note: Track caged (guitar-caged), step 3: the E and A shapes together: one chord in both shapes in three keys, then the 1, 4 and 5 chords in one area of the neck, once with the 1 chord in the E shape and once with it in the A shape.

exercise.title: E and A shapes: one chord twice, then 1 4 5
exercise.why: The E shape has its root on the low E string and the A shape has it on the A string, so in one area of the neck the two shapes give you three different chords: the 1, 4 and 5 of a key.

cells.text:
Press Play on the two chord panels below to hear the chord in the E shape and in the A shape. Play one, then the other, and say which string holds the root each time.
Then try another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key.
When you change the key, both shapes slide along the neck, and the root stays on the low E string in the E shape and on the A string in the A shape.

Press a chord box below to hear A, D and E as barre chords in one area of the neck. Then press Play under them to start the metronome, and strum down on every beat.
A, the 1 chord, is in the E shape. D and E, the 4 and the 5, are both in the A shape.

Press a chord box below to hear D, G and A as barre chords. Then press Play under them to start the metronome, and strum down on every beat.
When the 1 chord is in the A shape, the 4 and the 5 are both in the E shape. Keep going until you see where the 4 and 5 are before you leave the 1.
